explanation: The Pan-American Highway, which otherwise links Alaska with southern Argentina, stops on either side of the gap, so drivers ship their cars around it.

claims.text: The Darién Gap lies between Colombia and Panama.
Costa Rica does not border Colombia, and Colombia's borders with Venezuela and Ecuador do not cross the Darién Gap.
No road crosses the Darién Gap.
The Pan-American Highway is broken at the Darién Gap and otherwise runs from Alaska to southern Argentina.
Drivers on the Pan-American Highway ship their vehicles around the Darién Gap.

The schema requires a reviewBy date for slow items, so I entered 1 October 2028 as a suggestion; the editor sets the final date at acceptance. Regional: The Darién Gap is known to travellers and from the news worldwide; the map reasoning (what lies between Colombia and Central America) works anywhere. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight apostrophes, explanation of 24 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. Counterintuitive: false. Doubts: the item says nothing about migration through the gap, which is a sensitive and changing subject.
